<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">It remains to prove that the drawing of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline"><mi>G</mi></math> satisfies the conditions stated in Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem8" title="Proposition 8. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>.
Conditions (A) and (C) are shown to hold in Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem9" title="Proposition 9. ‣ Proof. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>
while (B) is handled in Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem10" title="Proposition 10. ‣ Proof. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.
Note that in Condition (C) there is a symmetry between the two edges, namely, the cyclic order can also be written as <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\gamma^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in},\alpha^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Therefore it is enough to prove, say, that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\gamma^{\rm out},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))\neq d(\beta^{\rm in},(%
\gamma^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in}))" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> holds for the given cyclic order of the endpoints, this is shown in the following Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem9" title="Proposition 9. ‣ Proof. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 9</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If the cyclic of order of <math id="Thmtheorem9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in},\gamma^{\rm out}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup></mrow></math> and <math id="Thmtheorem9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta^{\rm in}" display="inline"><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup></math> along <math id="Thmtheorem9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline"><mi>c</mi></math> is either 
<br class="ltx_break"><math id="Thmtheorem9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in},\gamma^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> or <math id="Thmtheorem9.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha^{\rm out},\gamma^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in},\delta^{\rm in})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, then <math id="Thmtheorem9.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\gamma^{\rm out},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))\neq d(\beta^{\rm in},(%
\gamma^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in}))" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Orient <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> such that they enter the interior of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline"><mi>c</mi></math> at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta^{\rm in}" display="inline"><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm out}" display="inline"><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup></math>, respectively (recall that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\neq\gamma" display="inline"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></math>).
We will show that if <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\gamma^{\rm out},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=2" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, then <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\beta^{\rm in},(\gamma^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in}))=1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. A symmetric argument (reflect the arrangement and switch the role of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> and also of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math>) shows that if <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\beta^{\rm in},(\gamma^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in}))=1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, then <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\gamma^{\rm out},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=2" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>. Together, these two assertions imply the claim.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Suppose that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\gamma^{\rm out},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=2" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>. This means
that as we follow <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> starting from <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm out}" display="inline"><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup></math> it intersects <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> before it intersects <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>. Let <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math> denote this first intersection point of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> (see Figure <a href="#S3.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ Proof. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>).
We will show that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\beta^{\rm in},x]_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math> does not intersect <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math>, and hence <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\beta^{\rm in},(\gamma^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in}))=1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> be the closed curve which consists of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},x]_{\gamma}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\beta^{\rm in},x]_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}]_{c}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub></math>.
We claim that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> is a simple curve that is not crossed by any of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math>, and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Consider first <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> and observe that it does not cross itself nor can it cross <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},x]_{\gamma}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></math> by the definition of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math>.
From Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem6" title="Proposition 6. ‣ Proof. ‣ 2 Some terminology and tools ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, it follows that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta^{\rm out}\in(\beta^{\rm in},\alpha^{\rm out})_{c}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow></math> and therefore <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> does not cross <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}]_{c}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub></math>, and hence it does not cross <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Next, consider <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> and observe that it does not cross itself nor can it cross <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}]_{c}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub></math> since it follows from Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem6" title="Proposition 6. ‣ Proof. ‣ 2 Some terminology and tools ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm in}\in(\delta^{\rm in},\gamma^{\rm out})_{c}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow></math>.
Therefore, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> is a simple curve (recall that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\gamma^{\rm out},x)_{\gamma}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></math> cannot intersect by the definition of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math>).
Let <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> be the “triangular” region which is bounded by <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> and is to the right of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> (and to the left of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline"><mi>c</mi></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Returning to <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math>, it remains to show that it cannot intersect <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta^{\rm in},x)_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math>.
Suppose for contradiction that it does intersect <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta^{\rm in},x)_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math> at a point <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math>.
Then either <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> enters <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math> or it leaves <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math>.
In the first case, following <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> from <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math>, it must leave <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> since the part of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> just before <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm out}" display="inline"><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup></math> lies outside <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math>.
However, this means that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> must cross <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> and hence <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta^{\rm in},x)_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math> at another point which is impossible since <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> already intersect at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p6.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math>, see Figure <a href="#S3.F9.sf1" title="In Figure 9 ‣ Proof. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9(a)</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F9" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="S3.F9.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="AandC-2.pdf2svg.svg" id="S3.F9.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" width="197" height="137" style="width: 394px; height: unset; max-width: 100%"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">If <math id="S3.F9.sf1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> enters <math id="S3.F9.sf1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> at <math id="S3.F9.sf1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math>, then it must intersect <math id="S3.F9.sf1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta^{\rm in},x)_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math> once more.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</div>
<div class="ltx_flex_break"></div>
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="S3.F9.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="AandC-3.pdf2svg.svg" id="S3.F9.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" width="197" height="137" style="width: 394px; height: unset; max-width: 100%"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">If <math id="S3.F9.sf2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> leaves <math id="S3.F9.sf2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> at <math id="S3.F9.sf2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math>, then <math id="S3.F9.sf2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> enters <math id="S3.F9.sf2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> at <math id="S3.F9.sf2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math> and must cross <math id="S3.F9.sf2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> at some other point.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</div>
</div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Illustrations for the proof of Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem9" title="Proposition 9. ‣ Proof. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>: when following <math id="S3.F9.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> into the interior of <math id="S3.F9.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline"><mi>c</mi></math> we meet <math id="S3.F9.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> sooner than <math id="S3.F9.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> at a point <math id="S3.F9.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math>. Suppose for contradiction that <math id="S3.F9.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> intersects <math id="S3.F9.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\beta^{\rm in},x]_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math> at another point <math id="S3.F9.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math>. Each pseudocircle’s label is placed within the digon-region associated with that pseudocircle.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Considering the second case, if <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> leaves <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math>, then it implies that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> enters <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math>, which in turn implies that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> is also entering <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math> (otherwise <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> would touch at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math> which is impossible), see Figure <a href="#S3.F9.sf2" title="In Figure 9 ‣ Proof. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9(b)</span></a>.
However, following <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> from <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math>, we would have to cross <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> since the part of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> just before <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta^{\rm in}" display="inline"><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup></math> lies outside <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math>.
Since we have already observed that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> does not cross <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> we conclude that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> does not cross <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p7.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> either.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We now show that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> cannot intersect <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math>.
By the definition of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math> it cannot intersect <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},x]_{\gamma}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></math>.
By Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem6" title="Proposition 6. ‣ Proof. ‣ 2 Some terminology and tools ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> we have <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\rm in}\in(\beta^{\rm in},\alpha^{\rm out})_{c}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow></math>
and it follows that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> cannot intersect <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}]_{c}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub></math>.
Finally, if <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> crosses <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\beta^{\rm in},x]_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math>, then it must cross it twice since <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> does not cross the other parts of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math>.
The digon formed by <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> must lie outside of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> since <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> lies outside the digon-region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math>.
Consequently, apart from its subarc that bounds this digon <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> is contained in <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math>.
However, this is impossible since then <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p8.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> do not intersect.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We are now ready to show that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> cannot intersect <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\beta^{\rm in},x]_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math> which would imply that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\beta^{\rm in},(\gamma^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in}))=1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
Assume to the contrary that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> intersects <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\beta^{\rm in},x]_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math>.
Notice that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta^{\rm in},\delta^{\rm out},\gamma^{\rm out}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup></mrow></math>, and
<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta^{\rm in}" display="inline"><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup></math> appear in this cyclic order on <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline"><mi>c</mi></math>. This follows from Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem6" title="Proposition 6. ‣ Proof. ‣ 2 Some terminology and tools ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and the assumptions of the claim.
This implies that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> does not intersect <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}]_{c}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub></math>.
It follows that the two simple closed curves <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> must either cross twice or four times, since crossing six times or more would imply that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> intersects <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> or <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> more than twice.
If <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> cross four times, then <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> crosses twice each of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\beta^{\rm in},x]_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},x]_{\gamma}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></math>.
Therefore, the only part of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math>
that is outside the digon-region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> and the digon-region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> must be in <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math>.
The curves <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> cannot cross in the digon-region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math>, because <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> form a digon. Similarly, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> cannot cross in the digon-region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> because <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> form a digon. Since <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> is disjoint from <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline"><mi>T</mi></math> we conclude that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> do not intersect which is a contradiction.
We reach a similar contradiction in the case where <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> crosses <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math> precisely at two points that happen to be on <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\beta^{\rm in},x]_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math>, once again <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m42" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p9.m43" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> cannot intersect.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">It remains to consider the case where <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> crosses <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\beta^{\rm in},x]_{\beta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub></math> once
and crosses <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},x]_{\gamma}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></math> once.
The latter implies that either <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math> or <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm out}" display="inline"><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup></math> belong to the digon formed by <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math>, which is impossible since neither <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> nor <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline"><mi>c</mi></math> intersects this digon.
<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p10.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 10</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\rm out},\gamma^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup></mrow></math> and <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta^{\rm in}" display="inline"><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup></math> appear in this cyclic order along <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline"><mi>c</mi></math>, then we have <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\gamma^{\rm out},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=d(\delta^{\rm in},(%
\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Orient <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> such that they enter the interior region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline"><mi>c</mi></math> at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm out}" display="inline"><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta^{\rm in}" display="inline"><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup></math>, respectively.
Recall that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline"><mi>c</mi></math> is oriented counterclockwise and its interior region lies to its left.
Thus, the digon-region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> lies to its left whereas the digon-region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> lies to its right.
Let <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2}\}=\delta\cap\alpha" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{B^{\prime}_{1},B^{\prime}_{2}\}=\delta\cap\beta" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, such that the cyclic order of these four points along <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> is <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2},B^{\prime}_{1},B^{\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> (since <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> form a digon it follows from Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem6" title="Proposition 6. ‣ Proof. ‣ 2 Some terminology and tools ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{1}^{\prime}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> must be consecutive and so are <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math>).
Similarly, let <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{A^{\prime\prime}_{1},A^{\prime\prime}_{2}\}=\gamma\cap\alpha" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{B^{\prime\prime}_{1},B^{\prime\prime}_{2}\}=\gamma\cap\beta" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, such that the cyclic order of these four points along <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> is <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime\prime}_{1},A^{\prime\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{1},B^{\prime\prime%
}_{2}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Considering the cyclic order of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></math> along <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> (under some orientation of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>), it follows
from Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem6" title="Proposition 6. ‣ Proof. ‣ 2 Some terminology and tools ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> that the first two are consecutive and so are the last two (since <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> form a digon).
Therefore, if we orient <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> such that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> follows <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math>, then the cyclic order of those four points is either <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{1},A^{\prime\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> or <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We claim that the former is impossible.
Indeed, suppose that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></math> appear in this cyclic order on <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>.
Note that it follows from the cyclic order on <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> (resp., <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math>) that both of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> (resp., <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></math>) must be in the same region (interior or exterior) of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>.
If <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{1},B^{\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></math> are in the exterior of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>, then
either <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[A^{\prime\prime}_{1},A^{\prime\prime}_{2}]_{\alpha}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>α</mi></msub></math> or <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[A_{1}^{\prime},A^{\prime}_{2}]_{\alpha}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>α</mi></msub></math> is contained in the intersection of the digon-regions of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> (see Figure <a href="#S3.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ Proof. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>), which is impossible.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F10" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="four-points-on-alpha.pdf2svg.svg" id="S3.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" width="393" height="127" style="width: 786px; height: unset; max-width: 100%"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Suppose that <math id="S3.F10.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{1},A^{\prime\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> appear in this cyclic order on <math id="S3.F10.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.F10.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{1},B^{\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.F10.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></math> are in the exterior of <math id="S3.F10.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>. Then the intersection of the digon-region of <math id="S3.F10.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> (which is to its right) and the digon-region of <math id="S3.F10.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> (which is to its left) contains either <math id="S3.F10.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[A^{\prime\prime}_{1},A^{\prime\prime}_{2}]_{\alpha}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>α</mi></msub></math> or <math id="S3.F10.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2}]_{\alpha}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>α</mi></msub></math> which is impossible.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">By a symmetric argument, it is impossible that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{1},B^{\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math>, and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></math> are in the interior of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>.
Therefore, either <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> are in the digon-region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> or <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></math> are there. However, this implies that the subarc of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> in the digon-region of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> intersects either <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> or <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> which is impossible since <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> form a digon.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Thus <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> appear in this cyclic order on <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>, and similarly, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{1},B^{\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> appear in this cyclic order on <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> if it is oriented such that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{2}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> immediately follows <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}_{1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math>.
Next, we redraw <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> close to the digon it forms with <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> such that these two pseudocircles become disjoint (see Figure <a href="#S3.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ Proof. ‣ 3.3 Independent edges cross evenly ‣ 3 Proof of Theorem 2 ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>).
In a similar way, we redraw <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> such that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> become disjoint.
Note that no other intersection points but <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\cap\beta" display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma\cap\delta" display="inline"><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></math> are destroyed and no new intersection points are introduced.
Therefore, the vertex set of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\cal{A}}(\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\})" display="inline"><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is precisely <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{A^{\prime}_{1},A^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{1},A^{\prime\prime}_{2},B^{%
\prime}_{1},B^{\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{1},B^{\prime\prime}_{2}\}" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></math> and its edge set consists of the edges

If <math id="S3.F11.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\gamma^{\rm out},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=2" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.F11.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\delta^{\rm in},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, then <math id="S3.F11.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm out}\in(A^{\prime\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{2})_{\gamma}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.F11.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta^{\rm in}\in(B^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime}_{2})_{\delta}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>δ</mi></msub></mrow></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Note that <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\gamma^{\rm out},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\delta^{\rm in},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=2" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> iff <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm out}\in(B^{\prime\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{2})_{\gamma}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta^{\rm in}\in(A^{\prime}_{2},B^{\prime}_{2})_{\delta}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>δ</mi></msub></mrow></math>.
Similarly, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\gamma^{\rm out},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=2" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(\delta^{\rm in},(\alpha^{\rm out},\beta^{\rm in}))=1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> iff <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm out}\in(A^{\prime\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{2})_{\gamma}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta^{\rm in}\in(B^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime}_{2})_{\delta}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>δ</mi></msub></mrow></math>.
Suppose for contradiction that one of these cases holds.
Then, on the one hand, there is a curve, namely <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\gamma^{\rm out},\delta^{\rm in}]_{c}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub></math>, which connects <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\rm out}" display="inline"><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>out</mi></msup></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta^{\rm in}" display="inline"><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>in</mi></msup></math> while not crossing any of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline"><mi>δ</mi></math> (this follows from the given cyclic order and Proposition <a href="#Thmtheorem6" title="Proposition 6. ‣ Proof. ‣ 2 Some terminology and tools ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>).
However, on the other hand, there is no face of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\cal{A}}(\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\})" display="inline"><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> whose boundary contains segments of both <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B^{\prime\prime}_{2},A^{\prime\prime}_{2})_{\gamma}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(A^{\prime}_{2},B^{\prime}_{2})_{\delta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>δ</mi></msub></math>
or segments of both <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(A^{\prime\prime}_{2},B^{\prime\prime}_{2})_{\gamma}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>γ</mi></msub></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B^{\prime}_{2},A^{\prime}_{2})_{\delta}" display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>δ</mi></msub></math>, contradicting the existence of a curve as above.
<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p6.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">This completes the proof of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Concluding remarks</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">What can we say about drawings on other surfaces? For example, we can draw <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{7}" display="inline"><msub><mi>K</mi><mn>7</mn></msub></math> on the torus, which implies the existence of 7 curves such that they pairwise form a digon, giving us 21 digons in total. This suggests that we need a significantly different approach since an argument based on the embeddability of the double cover would give roughly <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2n" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> as an upper bound.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem11" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_problem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Problem 11</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">What is the maximum number of digons in a pairwise intersecting family of pseudocircles on a closed
orientable connected surface <math id="Thmtheorem11.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline"><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></math> of genus g?</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We note that graphs with planar bipartite double covers were extensively studied in topological graph theory, see for example the works of Negami <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>, <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>. Negami also considered general covers of graphs and formulated the following nice conjecture:</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem12" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_conjecture">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Conjecture 12</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Negami 1988)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">A graph <math id="Thmtheorem12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline"><mi>G</mi></math> has a finite planar cover if and only if <math id="Thmtheorem12.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline"><mi>G</mi></math> embeds in the projective plane.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Indeed, with some extra work, one can show that digon graphs are embeddable in the projective plane, but we omit the proof.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Another natural question is to consider the number of triangles in intersecting pseudocircle arrangements. Felsner and Scheucher <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite> showed that the maximal number of triangles is <math id="S4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2n^{2}/3+O(n)" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>, and this is asymptotically tight. In their proof, they use the bound <math id="S4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(n)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite> for the maximum number of digons in pairwise intersecting arrangements of pseudocircles. By applying Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> instead, we achieve the following improvement for simple arrangements.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem13" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 13</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem13.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Every simple arrangement of <math id="Thmtheorem13.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\geqslant 4" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⩾</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> pairwise intersecting pseudocircles has at most <math id="Thmtheorem13.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{2}{3}n^{2}" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> triangles.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">On the other hand, triangles are unavoidable, they showed that there are at least <math id="S4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2n/3" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> triangles and made the subsequent conjecture.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem14" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_conjecture">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Conjecture 14</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem14.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Every pairwise intersecting arrangement of <math id="Thmtheorem14.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\geqslant 3" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⩾</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> pseudocircles has at least <math id="Thmtheorem14.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n-1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> triangles.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">On a final remark, we were able to extend our proof of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ The Maximum Number of Digons Formed by Pairwise Intersecting Pseudocircles" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> to nontrivial pairwise intersecting arrangements of pseudocircles. However, it involves dealing with several delicate subcases. Therefore, we have chosen to omit the full proof here.</p>
</div>
</section>
